content_sections.heading: WBPSC Sub Surveyor Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: To meet the WBPSC Sub Surveyor eligibility, candidates must satisfy the qualification, age, language and certificate conditions below. Candidates must be Indian citizens or other nationals declared eligible by the Government of India. Ability to read, write and speak in Bengali is an essential requirement. It is not mandatory for candidates whose mother tongue is Nepali, unless specifically mentioned. The candidature of candidates with poor performance in the knowledge of Bengali test is liable to be cancelled. Candidates must fulfil the essential qualifications by the closing date of the online application. Candidates claiming EWS, SC, ST, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), Ex-Serviceman, MSP or PwBD status (40% and above) must hold the certificate from the competent authority of West Bengal, obtained within the closing date of applications. All degrees, diplomas and certificates must be from universities/institutions duly recognized by the competent authority. The WBPSC Sub Surveyor qualification can be met in either of the two ways given below. Where experience is prescribed, it means experience gained in full-time employment/research in the relevant field within the closing date of receipt of applications. The experience certificate from the Head of the Organization/Department or competent authority must mention the duration of employment (date, month and year), the field of experience, the basic pay and consolidated pay, and the nature of duties performed. Where only grading is awarded and no Division/Class, the exact percentage of marks and the conversion formula adopted are to be mentioned with documentary evidence, if required.

rows.qualification: (i) Passed Madhyamik Examination or equivalent, and (ii) 3 years' Diploma in Survey Engineering from any recognized institute (affiliated by AICTE or West Bengal State Council of Technical Education)

(i) Passed Madhyamik Examination or equivalent, (ii) 2 years' certificate course for Surveyor from a recognized Industrial Training Institute, and (iii) 1 year's experience in Survey and Settlement work based on modern survey techniques and conversant in differential Global Positioning System (DGPS) and/or Electronic Total Stations (ETS) technology to carry out modern methods of surveying, from any Government empanelled organization or from an Indian Geographic Information System (GIS)/Surveying Company recognized under the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme, Department of Land Resources, Government of India, having at least 3 years' experience in preparation of large scale mapping and land records

content_sections.heading: WBPSC Sub Surveyor Selection Process
content_sections.text: The WBPSC Sub Surveyor selection process is a written examination of two papers. The final merit list is prepared on the basis of the marks obtained in Paper-II only. The notification also refers to Document Verification, but does not give its schedule. Qualifying marks are fixed at 30% of the marks allotted for Paper-I. The Commission has the discretion to fix the qualifying marks in Paper-II. Marks in Paper-II are taken into consideration only for candidates who attain 30% marks in Paper-I. There is negative marking of 0.25 mark for each wrong answer in the MCQ-type Paper-II. If two or more candidates get equal marks in Paper-II, preference is given to the senior candidate by date of birth. Marks are electronically captured from the scanned OMR sheet using uniform customized software, without manual intervention. Objections to the model answers displayed on the website must be filed strictly within the specified time limit. Paper-II, Elementary Mathematics: Arithmetic, algebra, geometry, trigonometry and mensuration, as per the standard of Madhyamik or equivalent examination. Paper-II, Survey Engineering: As per the standard of Diploma examination.

content_sections.heading: Documents and Certificates for WBPSC Sub Surveyor Recruitment
content_sections.text: One Photo ID, to be mentioned in the application form with its number and issuing authority: Madhyamik or equivalent certificate bearing photograph, Passport, PAN card, EPIC (voter ID card), Driving license, Aadhaar card, or any other ID proof issued by the State or Central Government. The same original photo ID must be brought to the examination venue. Madhyamik or equivalent certificate (for age and qualification) and the Diploma, or the ITI certificate with experience certificates, as applicable EWS: Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed format (Annexure-C), issued by the Additional District Magistrate in charge of development matters of the district, or the District Welfare Officer, Kolkata and Ex-officio Joint Director, BCW & TD for Kolkata. Renewed/revalidated certificates must be submitted prior to the examination and at the time of appointment. SC, ST and OBC (Non-Creamy Layer): Certificate issued by the Sub-Divisional Officer of the sub-division concerned, or in Kolkata by the authorities named in the notification. OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates must submit renewed/revalidated certificates prior to the examination and at the time of appointment. PwBD: Disability certificate from a Medical Board constituted at Government Medical College Hospitals in Kolkata, District Hospitals and Sub-Divisional Hospitals. For scribe and/or compensatory time, the Appendix-I certificate regarding physical limitation to write from the Chief Medical Officer/Medical Superintendent of a Government Health Care Institution. Meritorious Sportspersons (MSP): Certificate from the competent authority and the duly filled and signed FORM 1/2/3/4, as applicable, at the time of document verification. The sports covered are Athletics, Badminton, Basket Ball, Cricket, Football, Hockey, Swimming, Table Tennis, Volley Ball, Tennis, Weight Lifting, Wrestling, Boxing, Cycling, Gymnastics, Judo, Rifle Shooting, Kabaddi, Kho-Kho and Archery. Ex-Servicemen: Certificate from the Army/Air Force/Naval Headquarters showing the date of joining, the period of service and the date of release or completion of service. Candidates with Benchmark Disabilities who have a limitation in writing may be allowed a scribe. The scribe should have an educational qualification one step below that of the candidate. Candidates producing a valid Appendix-I are allowed compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour. The details of the scribe cannot be added after final submission of the application. For Blindness, Locomotor Disability (both arms affected, BA) and cerebral palsy, the scribe facility is given if the candidate desires it.

faq.question: Q1. What is the organization conducting this recruitment?
faq.answer: The West Bengal Public Service Commission (WBPSC) is conducting the recruitment for the Sub-Surveyor position under advertisement number 22/2024 for filling up 1145 vacancies.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available for the Sub-Surveyor post?
faq.answer: A total of 1145 vacancies have been officially announced by the West Bengal Public Service Commission for the Sub-Surveyor recruitment drive.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification required for WBPSC Sub-Surveyor?
faq.answer: Candidates must have passed the Madhyamik Examination or equivalent, along with a 3 years Diploma in Survey Engineering or a 2 years certificate course for Surveyor with 1 year experience.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for this recruitment?
faq.answer: Applicants must be between 21 and 45 years of age as on 01.01.2024. Age relaxations are provided for reserved categories as per government rules.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary scale for the Sub-Surveyor post?
faq.answer: Selected candidates will receive a salary as per Level - 7, ranging from Rs. 24,700 to Rs. 63,900 per month along with admissible allowances.

faq.question: Q6. When does the online application process start and end?
faq.answer: The online application process commences on 20 October 2026 and concludes on 9 November 2026. Fee payment must also be completed by 9 November 2026.

faq.question: Q7. Is there an application fee for WBPSC Sub-Surveyor?
faq.answer: Yes, General and OBC candidates are required to pay Rs. 110/- plus service charges, whereas SC/ST candidates of West Bengal and PwBD candidates are exempt from fee payment.

faq.question: Q8. What is the selection process for this post?
faq.answer: The selection process comprises Paper-I (Conventional type Bengali/Nepali test) and Paper-II (Objective type MCQs on English, Elementary Mathematics, and Survey Engineering), followed by a final merit list.

faq.question: Q9. Is there any edit window available for corrections?
faq.answer: Yes, an edit window for making necessary corrections in the submitted online application form will remain available from 11 November 2026 to 16 November 2026.

faq.question: Q10. Where can I apply for WBPSC Sub-Surveyor Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Eligible and interested candidates can submit their online applications through the official WBPSC website at https://psc.wb.gov.in before the closing date.
